economics.bop-analyse-1.0001.all: High demand for imports (electronics, cars) raises import spending on current account; possibly high incomes/strong currency; falling manufactured exports reduce export revenue (loss of competitiveness, higher costs, strong exchange rate) -> trade in goods deficit widens; persistent 7 yrs suggests structural cause.

economics.competition-analyse-2.0003.all: Monopoly can set high prices (price maker) reducing consumer surplus; little choice, no alternative supplier; poor service/quality as no incentive to improve; less innovation; supernormal profits at consumers' expense.

economics.competition-assess-2.0001.all: For: lower prices, better service, choice, efficiency/innovation. Against: natural monopoly / economies of scale lost, high infrastructure costs, duplication, firms may cherry-pick; regulation alternative. Judgement depends on regulation and barriers.

economics.competition-assess-3.0004.all: Negative: lower sales/profit for local shops, closures (15%), job losses; positive: forces efficiency, innovation, niche/personal service, move online. Depends on shops' ability to differentiate.

economics.competition-evaluate-2.0003.all: Benefits: lower fares, better service, efficiency, innovation. Costs: natural monopoly, lost economies of scale, infrastructure duplication, unprofitable routes cut, safety. Alternative: regulate/price cap. Judgement depends.

economics.competition-evaluate-3.0001.all: Lower prices reduce revenue/profit of local shops, 23% closed, unemployment; but efficiency, innovation, differentiation, online channels; consumers benefit. Depends on firm type, size, adaptability.

economics.competition-explain.0002.all: Non-price competition e.g. advertising/branding or better network/coverage/features -> attracts customers from rivals -> increases market share; oligopoly avoid price wars.

economics.competition-mcq-class.0007.all: D - There are many buyers and sellers

economics.costs-analyse-1.0005.all: Fuel 18% rise and wage rises increase variable/total costs; with small profit, may become loss; may raise prices, reducing demand; or cut costs/staff; lower profit for investment.

economics.costs-analyse-3.0003.all: Profit = TR - TC; TC rose faster than 15% TR rise e.g. rising raw material/wages, fixed costs; perhaps price cuts to raise sales increased volume but lower margin; so profit fell.

economics.costs-assess-1.0003.all: For: maintain profit margins, cover 31% fuel rise, rivals face same costs. Against: depends on PED; elastic demand -> revenue falls, lose customers to rivals; alternatives cut costs, efficiency, fuel-efficient vehicles. Judgement on PED/competition.

economics.costs-assess-3.0001.all: Raise prices (depends on PED), cut costs (cheaper suppliers, efficiency, technology), increase sales via marketing, economies of scale; evaluate trade-offs (quality, demand). Judgement.

economics.costs-data.0005.b: Higher fuel and wage costs raise TC; small profit may become loss; may need to raise prices, losing customers; cut costs/investment.
economics.costs-data.0005.c: For raise: protect margins, rivals face same costs, inelastic demand. Against: elastic demand/competition lose customers; alternatives: efficiency, fuel hedging. Judgement depends on PED.

economics.costs-evaluate-1.0003.all: As costs-assess-1: price rise maintains margin if demand inelastic; risk losing customers if elastic/competitive; alternatives cost cutting, fuel-efficient vehicles; judgement depends on PED, competitors, duration of fuel rise.

economics.costs-evaluate-2.0005.all: For: double output, economies of scale, lower average costs, meet demand. Against: higher fixed costs/risk, needs demand for doubled output, finance cost, break-even rises. Judgement depends on demand.

economics.costs-evaluate-3.0003.all: Raise price (PED), reduce costs, increase sales, economies of scale, differentiate; evaluate each; judgement.

economics.demand-diagram.0006.all: Bread cheaper -> more bread demanded -> demand for butter (complement) rises: D shifts right to D1; new higher price P1 and higher quantity Q1.

economics.environment-explain.0003.all: Tax raises cost of production for polluting firms -> incentive to cut emissions/switch to cleaner tech or reduce output -> less carbon, internalises external cost.

economics.exchange-data.0013.b: Uncertainty over revenue from exports and cost of imports; hard to price contracts/plan; profit margins vary; deters investment; hedging costs.
economics.exchange-data.0013.c: For intervention: stability, confidence, investment, trade. Against: uses reserves, interest rate changes affect inflation/growth, may fail against market forces; firms can hedge. Judgement.

economics.exchange-explain.0003.all: Depreciation makes imports dearer in euros -> raw material costs rise -> higher costs of production, lower profit margins or higher prices.

economics.externalities-analyse-1.0001.all: Reduces negative externalities: cleaner beaches/rivers, less harm to wildlife, tourism benefits, lower clean-up costs; but enforcement costs and illegal use reduce benefit.

economics.externalities-assess-1.0003.all: Works: cleaner beaches, simple, clear. Limitations: enforcement costly, illegal use continues, no revenue, substitutes may pollute; alternatives taxes/charges. Judgement.

economics.externalities-data.0015.b: Third parties benefit: herd immunity, fewer infections, lower healthcare costs, fewer working days lost; social benefit > private benefit, underconsumed without subsidy.
economics.externalities-data.0015.c: For: corrects underconsumption, positive externalities, long term savings. Against: opportunity cost, tax funding, may have risen anyway, diminishing returns at high rate. Judgement.

economics.externalities-evaluate-1.0001.all: As assess: effective cleaner environment; but enforcement costly, evasion, no revenue, inflexible; compare tax/levy/education. Judgement.

economics.fiscal-data.0003.b: Spending cuts reduce public services quality; higher sales tax raises prices, reduces real income/disposable income, lower consumption; regressive effect on poor.
economics.fiscal-data.0003.c: For reduce: debt 75% interest costs, confidence, future burden. Against: contractionary, unemployment, lower growth, may worsen deficit. Judgement depends on economic cycle.

economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0006.all: Low wages/exploitation, poor conditions; profits repatriated; dependency on MNCs who may relocate (footloose); environmental damage; little skill transfer.

economics.globalisation-assess-3.0002.all: Benefits: employment 4m, women's incomes, exports, FDI, skills. Costs: low wages, conditions, repatriated profits, footloose. Judgement.

economics.globalisation-evaluate-3.0002.all: As assess, fuller evaluation; judgement depends on wages relative to alternatives, regulation.

economics.globalisation-explain.0001.all: Creates 5,000 jobs -> lower unemployment -> incomes and spending rise, multiplier/tax revenue.

economics.globalisation-state-class.0002.all: Profits repatriated to home country (or exploitation of workers / environmental damage).
